Every year hundreds of cheetah cubs are stolen from the wild, decimating the dwindling population of Africa's most endangered big cat. For every five cubs that are taken, only one survives. They are then smuggled into the Middle East to be sold as an exotic pet.
Not A Pet looks at the illegal wildlife pet trade, and the role social media plays in the parading and trading of exotic animals online. This episode focuses on great apes and monkeys.

Tigers might be the most endangered big cat in the world, but they are a common sight in captivity, often exploited for petting opportunities, circuses, or kept as exotic pets to flaunt as status symbols.

Live reptiles and amphibians are hugely popular amongst collectors; the rarer the species, the more valuable it is in the exotic pet trade. But many of the animals found in this trade have in fact come from the wild, causing many populations to be pushed towards extinction.

Amazonian apex predator and true American hero. Three million years in the making but now on the verge of breaking. Their penchant for predation holds the key to rewilding tropical ecosystems. Learn why these natural born healers deserve our respect.
